posts.title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
posts.imageAlt: A tall stack of golden buttermilk pancakes with butter and maple syrup
posts.seoTitle: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes (Ready in 20 Minutes) | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Make tall, fluffy buttermilk pancakes at home with pantry staples. A simple weekend breakfast recipe ready in 20 minutes.
posts.excerpt: Tall, soft pancakes with crisp edges, made with pantry staples in 20 minutes.
posts.intro: These are the pancakes we make every Sunday. Buttermilk makes them tender and helps them rise tall, and resting the batter for five minutes gives you the fluffiest stack.
ingredients: 3 tbsp melted butter, plus more for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
Rest the batter for 5 minutes while you heat a buttered pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup of batter per pancake. Flip when bubbles form on top, about 2 minutes, then cook 1 minute more.
posts.tip: No buttermilk? Stir 2 tbsp lemon juice into 2 cups of milk and wait 5 minutes.

posts.title: Masala Omelette
posts.imageAlt: A folded masala omelette with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander
posts.seoTitle: Masala Omelette Recipe: Indian Street-Style Eggs | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: A spicy Indian masala omelette with onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander. Ready in 10 minutes and perfect with buttered toast.
posts.excerpt: Street-style Indian omelette packed with onion, tomato, chilli and coriander.
posts.intro: This is the omelette sold at street stalls all over India, usually tucked inside soft buttered bread. It takes ten minutes and wakes you up better than coffee.
steps: Beat the eggs with turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat and pour in the egg mix.
Cook until the bottom is set, about 2 minutes, then flip or fold.
Cook 1 more minute and serve hot with toast.
posts.tip: Keep the vegetables finely chopped so the omelette holds together when you fold it.

posts.title: Overnight Oats with Berries
posts.imageAlt: A glass jar of overnight oats layered with yoghurt and fresh berries
posts.seoTitle: Overnight Oats with Berries: 5-Minute Make-Ahead Breakfast | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Creamy overnight oats with yoghurt, chia and fresh berries. Prep five jars on Sunday for an easy, healthy breakfast all week.
posts.excerpt: Five minutes of prep tonight, a creamy healthy breakfast tomorrow.
posts.intro: Overnight oats are the easiest healthy breakfast there is. Mix everything in a jar before bed and breakfast is waiting for you in the fridge.
steps: Add the oats, milk, yoghurt, chia seeds and honey to a jar.
Stir well, close the lid and refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
In the morning, stir again and add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
Top with berries and serve cold.
posts.tip: Use rolled oats, not instant oats. Instant oats turn mushy overnight.

posts.title: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
posts.imageAlt: Sourdough toast topped with smashed avocado and a soft poached egg
posts.seoTitle: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg (Foolproof Method) | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Crunchy sourdough, smashed avocado with lime and chilli, and a perfect poached egg. A 10-minute breakfast with a foolproof poaching method.
posts.excerpt: Smashed avocado, lime, chilli flakes and a runny poached egg on crunchy toast.
posts.intro: Good avocado toast is all about contrast: crunchy bread, creamy avocado, a squeeze of lime and an egg yolk that runs over everything.
steps: Toast the bread until deep golden.
Mash the avocado with lime juice, salt and pepper.
Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar.
Crack each egg into a cup, stir the water into a gentle swirl and slide the egg in. Cook 3 minutes.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with the egg and finish with chilli flakes.
posts.tip: The fresher the egg, the neater it poaches.

posts.title: Creamy Tomato Basil Soup
posts.imageAlt: A bowl of creamy tomato basil soup with a swirl of cream and fresh basil
posts.seoTitle: Creamy Tomato Basil Soup in 30 Minutes | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: A velvety tomato basil soup made with canned tomatoes in 30 minutes. Freezer friendly and perfect with a grilled cheese sandwich.
posts.excerpt: Velvety, comforting soup from canned tomatoes in 30 minutes.
posts.intro: Canned tomatoes make this soup possible any time of year. A little butter and cream round out the acidity and fresh basil makes it taste like summer.
steps: Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream and basil.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.
posts.tip: The soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Freeze it before adding the cream.

posts.title: Chicken Biryani
posts.imageAlt: A pot of layered chicken biryani with saffron rice and fried onions
posts.seoTitle: Easy Chicken Biryani at Home (Step-by-Step) | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Fragrant layered chicken biryani with marinated chicken, saffron rice and crispy onions. A step-by-step recipe that works in a regular pot.
posts.excerpt: Fragrant layers of spiced chicken and saffron rice, cooked in one pot.
posts.intro: Biryani looks hard but it is really three simple steps: marinate the chicken, par-boil the rice, then layer and steam. This version works in any heavy pot.
ingredients: A pinch of saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
steps: Marinate the chicken with yoghurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the chicken in a heavy pot with 1 tbsp ghee for 15 minutes until almost done.
Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes until 70% cooked, then drain.
Layer the rice over the chicken. Top with fried onions, herbs, saffron milk and the remaining ghee.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before opening.
posts.tip: Seal the lid with foil so no steam escapes. Steam is what cooks the top layer of rice.

posts.title: Paneer Tikka Wrap
posts.imageAlt: A paneer tikka wrap cut in half showing charred paneer, onions and mint chutney
posts.seoTitle: Paneer Tikka Wrap with Mint Chutney | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Smoky pan-charred paneer tikka rolled in a soft wrap with onions and mint chutney. A filling vegetarian lunch that packs well.
posts.excerpt: Smoky pan-charred paneer, crunchy onions and mint chutney in a soft wrap.
posts.intro: All the flavour of restaurant paneer tikka, made in a frying pan and rolled into a wrap you can take to work.
steps: Mix the yoghurt, tikka masala, chilli powder, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Coat the paneer.
Heat the oil in a pan on high heat and sear the paneer until charred on all sides.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Spread mint chutney on each tortilla, add the paneer and onion, and roll tightly.
Cut in half and serve, or wrap in foil to pack.
posts.tip: Pat the paneer dry before marinating so the marinade sticks.

posts.title: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
posts.imageAlt: A bowl of chickpea salad with cucumber, tomato, red onion, olives and feta
posts.seoTitle: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad (High Protein, No Cook) | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: A crunchy no-cook Mediterranean chickpea salad with cucumber, tomato, olives and feta. High in protein and keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
posts.excerpt: A crunchy, high-protein salad that tastes even better the next day.
posts.intro: This salad is made for meal prep. Chickpeas soak up the lemony dressing and the vegetables stay crunchy for days.
steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas and toss to coat.
Add the cucumber, tomato, onion and olives.
Top with feta just before serving.
posts.tip: If packing for later, keep the feta separate so it stays creamy.

posts.title: Classic Chocolate Brownies
posts.imageAlt: Squares of fudgy chocolate brownies with a crackly top
posts.seoTitle: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies with a Crackly Top | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Rich, fudgy chocolate brownies with a shiny crackly top, made in one bowl. The only brownie recipe you need.
posts.excerpt: Fudgy, rich, one-bowl brownies with that shiny crackly top.
posts.intro: The secret to the crackly top is whisking the sugar and eggs hard for a full minute. The secret to fudgy middles is taking them out of the oven a little early.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla hard for 1 minute until pale.
Whisk in the chocolate mix, then fold in the flour, cocoa and salt.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes until the centre is just set. Cool completely before cutting.
posts.tip: Cool the brownies fully, even overnight, for clean squares.

posts.title: Mango Lassi Popsicles
posts.imageAlt: Bright orange mango lassi popsicles on a tray with sliced mango
posts.metaDesc: Creamy mango lassi popsicles made with just mango, yoghurt and honey. A no-bake, kid-friendly summer dessert.
posts.excerpt: Three ingredients, no cooking, and the creamiest frozen treat of summer.
posts.intro: Everything you love about a mango lassi, frozen on a stick. Use ripe Alphonso mangoes if you can find them, or good canned mango pulp.
ingredients: 2 cups ripe mango, chopped (or mango pulp)
steps: Blend the mango, yoghurt, honey and cardamom until smooth.
Taste and add more honey if your mangoes are not very sweet.
Pour into popsicle moulds and add sticks.
Freeze for at least 6 hours. Run the moulds under warm water to release.
posts.tip: Leave a little space at the top of each mould. The mix expands as it freezes.

posts.title: Soft Gulab Jamun
posts.imageAlt: Soft gulab jamun soaking in rose and cardamom sugar syrup
posts.seoTitle: Soft Gulab Jamun with Milk Powder | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Soft, melt-in-the-mouth gulab jamun made with milk powder and soaked in rose cardamom syrup. Easy tips so they never crack.
posts.excerpt: Melt-in-the-mouth milk dumplings soaked in rose and cardamom syrup.
posts.intro: Gulab jamun made with milk powder are easier than the traditional khoya version and just as soft. Fry them slowly so they cook all the way through.
steps: Boil the sugar, water and cardamom for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the rose water.
Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda. Rub in the ghee.
Add milk a spoon at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Rest 5 minutes.
Roll into small crack-free balls.
Fry on low heat, stirring gently, until deep golden brown, about 6 minutes.
Drop the hot jamuns into the warm syrup and soak for at least 1 hour.
posts.tip: If the oil is too hot, the outside browns before the inside cooks. Low and slow is the rule.

posts.title: No-Bake Lemon Cheesecake Bars
posts.imageAlt: Creamy lemon cheesecake bars on a biscuit base with lemon zest
posts.seoTitle: No-Bake Lemon Cheesecake Bars (No Gelatin) | Spoonful
posts.metaDesc: Tangy no-bake lemon cheesecake bars on a buttery biscuit base. No oven and no gelatin, just chill overnight and slice.
posts.excerpt: A buttery biscuit base and tangy lemon filling. No oven required.
posts.intro: These bars set in the fridge with no gelatin, thanks to cream cheese and whipped cream. Make them the day before a party and just slice and serve.
steps: Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into a lined 20 cm tin. Chill 15 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar, lemon zest and juice until smooth.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the cream cheese mix.
Spread over the base and smooth the top.
Chill for at least 6 hours, then cut into bars.
posts.tip: Wipe the knife with a hot damp cloth between cuts for clean edges.

pages.title: About
pages.metaDesc: Spoonful is a home cooking blog with simple, tested recipes for breakfast, lunch and dessert. Meet the cook behind the recipes.
pages.content:
Spoonful started in a tiny rented kitchen with one pan, one pot and a lot of curiosity. Today it is a collection of simple, tested recipes that anyone can cook on a weeknight.

What you will find here

  • Breakfasts that take 20 minutes or less
  • Lunches that pack well for work and school
  • Desserts for every skill level, including plenty of no-bake treats

How we test recipes

Every recipe is cooked at least three times in a normal home kitchen, with normal home equipment, before it goes on the blog. If a step is confusing, we rewrite it.

Have a question or a recipe request? Get in touch.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.metaDesc: How Spoonful collects, uses and protects your information, including contact form messages and cookies.
pages.content:
This privacy policy explains what information Spoonful collects and how we use it.

Information we collect

When you send a message through our contact form, we collect your name, email address and message so we can reply to you. We do not sell or share this information.

Cookies

This site does not use advertising cookies. Our hosting provider may collect anonymous technical logs, such as IP address and browser type, to keep the site secure.

Your rights

You can ask us to see or delete any message you sent us. Use the contact page to make a request.

Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The latest version will always be on this page.
